notes: NY Fed figures (Citibank 42.8%, JPMorgan 29.5%, HSBC 12.6m/6.1%, Goldman 8.3m/4%, BNY Mellon 7.2m/3.5%, Morgan Stanley 4.8m + 2.8m = 3.7%, Deutsche 1.7m + 60,678 = 0.87%, Mizuho 819,344, ICBC 221,278) match the user's notes exactly and are verified against Institutional Investor (24 Feb 2020), which obtained the NY Fed 'Capital Stock Master Report' for year-end 2018 by FOIA. The article also gives Citibank 87.9m and JPMorgan 60.6m shares. No more recent named-holder figure was found.

No named-holder share data was found for the other 11 Federal Reserve Banks. The Fed does not publish holder-level stock registers. Call reports and the FR Y-9C do not break out Federal Reserve Bank stock by Reserve Bank in any source found here.

Fed governance: member banks elect Class A (representing member banks) and Class B (representing the public) directors; the Board of Governors appoints Class C directors (federalreserve.gov, 'About Reserve Bank directors'). Member banks elect six of nine head-office directors (St. Louis Fed, 14 Feb 2022). Dodd-Frank: the Fed's revised rules, effective 16 Dec 2010, say only Class B and C directors can appoint Reserve Bank presidents and first vice presidents, and Class A directors 'no longer have a role' (NY Fed press release, 22 Dec 2010, https://www.newyorkfed.org/newsevents/news/aboutthefed/2010/an101222). POGO (19 Oct 2011) reporting on GAO report d1218 (inferred to be GAO-12-18) attributes the change to Dodd-Frank. NY Fed presidential-search FAQ: the president is appointed by Class B and C directors with Board of Governors approval.

Fed stock rules: under 12 U.S.C. 287, a member bank subscribes 6% of a capital increase, half paid in and half subject to call; Reserve Bank shares 'shall not be transferred or hypothecated' (Cornell LII). The Fed FAQ says owning the stock is a condition of membership and is 'quite different from owning stock in a private company'.
NY Fed member-bank voting is grouped by size: e.g. the April 2022 special Class B election was voted only by the 30 Group 3 banks (capital and surplus under $40m) (NY Fed Circular, 15 Apr 2022).

Note on HQ data: per the Fed's Large Commercial Banks release (30 Jun 2026), Citibank N.A.'s main office is Sioux Falls, SD and JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A.'s is Columbus, OH, yet both held NY Fed stock in 2018 per the FOIA data. hq_city/hq_iso3 in holdings give the ultimate parent's HQ, not the bank's main office.
Mizuho Bank (USA) and ICBC USA are below the Large Commercial Banks threshold page range read; parent links come from FDIC resolution plans and Wikipedia.

Banca d'Italia: all 173 participants from the official list as at 30 Apr 2026 (total 300,000 quotas = EUR 7.5bn). The same page also posts a list as at 6 Mar 2026 (not used). The 5% cap equals 15,000 quotas: UniCredit holds exactly 15,000. Holder_type is assigned by name (pension funds / casse di previdenza, insurers, foundations, banks); verify edge cases. Eligible holders must be Italian banks, insurers, banking foundations, social security institutions or pension funds (Bank of Italy page). Parent groups for Italian holders were not researched.

Swiss National Bank: 100,000 registered shares (CHF 250 each), listed on SIX. At end-2025 cantons and cantonal banks held 51.0% of capital and 75.2% of voting shares. SNB names only five principal holders (four cantons plus Theo Siegert, Düsseldorf) and does not name any cantonal bank individually.

SARB: the primary register is no longer online (the Namibian Brief says it was removed in 2021). Named holders come from news articles citing the SARB Shareholder Index of 30 June 2022, so they are marked verified=false. The Brief also reports 16 German holders with about 91,850 shares combined and 16 British holders with about 14,000; these are not entered as holdings (https://thebrief.com.na/?p=26775). The SARB site was blocked to direct download; its shareholder page (via fetch) gives 2,000,000 shares, >800 holders, a 10,000-share cap, and voting only for SA residents at one vote per 200 shares.

CBRT: Class B shares are reserved for national banks operating in Türkiye, but the annual report table lists holders without their share class, so 'which national banks hold class B' cannot be stated per holder from this source. No privileged companies are among the shareholders.
Bank of Japan: no named private subscription-certificate holders are published; only the government's ~55% is recorded.
National Bank of Belgium: only the Belgian State (50%) is a notified holder; the other 50% floats on Euronext Brussels with no named major holder in the FSMA overview.

Bank of Greece: Greek State 8.93% (1,774,088 shares) is verified from a BoG Law 3556/2007 announcement (2011). The e-EFKA 12.44% figure is from Wikipedia, unsourced, and marked unverified. Before 2011, DEKA S.A. held 1,309,210 shares (6.59%) per BoG announcements of 2009 and 2010.

BIS: bis.org (accessed 24 Oct 2026) says 'The Bank's capital is held by central banks only' and lists 63 member central banks, including the ECB (iso3 given as EUU, a non-ISO placeholder). Private shareholders were removed when the EGM of 8 Jan 2001 approved a mandatory repurchase of all privately held shares at CHF 16,000 each. The Hague Arbitral Tribunal's final award (published 22 Sep 2003) added CHF 9,052.90 per share. bis.org gives the number of withdrawn private shares as 72,648 in one note and 72,638 in another. Before the buyout, central banks held 100% of voting rights and 86.27% of property rights (BIS note of 15 Sep 2000). Source: https://www.bis.org/about/legal/shares-withdrawal. No private shareholders remain.
